title: The impact of gut microbiota and metabolite-driven immune cell spatiotemporal dynamics on tumors

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《The impact of gut microbiota and metabolite-driven immune cell spatiotemporal dynamics on tumors》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · s0001-p4】Immune cells are essential in anti-tumor therapy. Notably, immune cell exhaustion, marked by the upregulation of immune checkpoint proteins (e.g., PD-1, CTLA-4, Tim-3, and Lag-3) on T cells, leads to T-cell dysfunction 29 and is a key mechanism driving the development and progression of malignant tumors. 30 , 31 Recent research has increasingly focused on the spatiotemporal dynamics of immune cells, considering their temporal, spatial, and functional characteristics. During ICI treatment, the clonal expansion of T cells is recognized as a hallmark of enhanced anti-tumor activity. With the advent of single-cell sequencing technologies, the distribution and cellular states of lymphocytes within the TME have been shown to correlate closely with cancer immune responses, exhibiting features of tumor-specific reactive T cells. 32 However, only a small fraction of tumor-infiltrating T cells are tumor-specific; the majority are “bystander T cells” that recognize non-tumor-related antigens, lacking activation or exhaustion markers, and thus fail to exert direct anti-tumor activity. 33 In addition, natural killer (NK) cells, central to innate immunity, play an irreplaceable role in non-specific anti-tumor immunity. Their functional activity is maintained in dynamic equilibrium through the regulation of multiple immune checkpoints on both the cell membrane and within the cytoplasm. The TME, as a complex and dynamic ecosystem, modulates NK cell functionality through factors such as hypoxia, metabolic reprogramming, and the secretion of immunosuppressive molecules, often inducing an exhausted phenotype. However, targeted interventions can restore their anti-tumor functions effectively. For instance, single-checkpoint blockade therapies, multi-checkpoint blockade therapies, and combination therapies targeting checkpoints such as NKG2A, TIGIT, and PD-1/PD-L1 have been developed and investigated, which hold great potential in reversing NK cell exhaustion and enhancing their anti-tumor efficacy. 34

In 2024, new cancer cases in China reached 3,246,625, with lung cancer being the most prevalent malignancy. 1 The host immune response plays a critical role in tumor cell elimination, and recent advances in cancer research have increasingly focused on immunotherapy and the host immune system. However, despite the promising efficacy of targeted anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapies, 2-8 a subset of patients remains unresponsive to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) treatments in clinical practice. 9

【Introduction · s0001-p1】Cancer has become one of the leading threats to human health, driven primarily by the abnormal proliferation and invasiveness of tumor cells. In 2024, new cancer cases in China reached 3,246,625, with lung cancer being the most prevalent malignancy. 1 The host immune response plays a critical role in tumor cell elimination, and recent advances in cancer research have increasingly focused on immunotherapy and the host immune system. However, despite the promising efficacy of targeted anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapies, 2-8 a subset of patients remains unresponsive to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) treatments in clinical practice. 9

【Introduction · s0001-p3】Pathogenic bacteria can induce chronic inflammation, and their metabolites, such as secondary bile acids, promote abnormal proliferation and malignant transformation of intestinal epithelial cells. Additionally, a reduction in short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) compromises intestinal barrier integrity and immune regulatory functions. Conversely, beneficial bacteria (e.g., Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus) exert anti-carcinogenic effects by regulating microbial homeostasis, degrading carcinogenic substances, and enhancing anti-tumor immunity. 10 For instance, the enrichment of pathogenic bacteria such as Escherichia coli and Bacteroides fragilis (enterotoxin-producing strains) has been associated with chronic inflammation and the release of pro-inflammatory and carcinogenic mediators. 18 Additionally, beneficial bacteria like Bifidobacterium have been shown to improve chemotherapy outcomes by alleviating inflammation and boosting mucosal immunity in cancer patients. 19 Existing studies demonstrate that the gut microbiota contributes to tumor initiation and progression by driving the spatiotemporal dynamics and functional plasticity of immune cells, thereby exerting anti-tumor immune effects within the tumor microenvironment (TME). 20-28

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《The impact of gut microbiota and metabolite-driven immune cell spatiotemporal dynamics on tumors》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · s0006-p1】Cancer remains one of the primary threats to human health in the modern era. Immunotherapy, particularly ICIs, has made remarkable strides in cancer treatment by harnessing the body’s anti-tumor immune response. However, not all patients benefit from immunotherapy, and some experience immune-related adverse events (irAEs). As a result, identifying reliable biomarkers to predict immune responses has become a key research focus.

【Conclusion · s0006-p2】Accumulating evidence highlights the role of the gut microbiota in modulating the TME by influencing the spatiotemporal dynamics and functional plasticity of immune cells, thereby regulating the host immune system and anti-tumor responses. Therefore, a comprehensive understanding of the crosstalk between the gut microbiota and the immune system is critical for advancing our knowledge of the entire anti-tumor process. This review systematically explores the relationship between anti-tumor immune responses and the spatiotemporal dynamics of immune cells from three dimensions. It also examines the gut microbiota-mediated dynamic changes in host immune cells, including proliferation, migration, recruitment, and functional transformation, while analyzing the effects of TME remodeling on tumor progression from multiple perspectives. However, the functional effects of one or more gut microbial taxa and their metabolites exhibit striking interhost heterogeneity. A case in point is Akkermansia muciniphila as discussed in this review, whose anti-tumor immune modulation is tightly associated with its relative abundance and features a dual regulatory role. From the optimization of tumor therapeutic strategies to the implementation of personalized precision interventions, the gut microbiota holds immense translational potential in oncology. Nevertheless, its clinical translation is plagued by multiple bottlenecks, which stands as one of the critical challenges demanding urgent breakthroughs at present. The comprehensive construction of personalized predictive and interventional models, coupled with the application of artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms to the in-depth integration and analysis of multi-omics data of the gut microbiota, will become the core direction of our future research.

【Figure 1. · f0001】Figure 1. Temporal dynamics of immune cells. Immune cell populations in the human body exhibit circadian fluctuations, which can influence the effectiveness of conventional treatments for patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

【Figure 2. · f0002】Figure 2. Spatial distribution of immune cells. The infiltration, migration, and recruitment of immune cells lead to inter-individual variability in their spatial distribution, which can serve as a predictive indicator of the efficacy of conventional tumor therapies. N20-CD8+ T cells: CD8+ T cells located within 20 μm of tumor cells.

【Figure 3. · f0003】Figure 3. Functional plasticity of immune cells. Immune cell functionality is regulated by various factors (e.g., intratumoral microbiota, gut microbiota, and metabolites). Immune cells in distinct functional states contribute differently to anti-tumor responses.
